# 3D Printing, CNC & Laser Cutting in Tehran, Iran | HyperFab

URL: https://hyperfabgroup.github.io/en/

Making a part is as simple as an upload

Choose process, material and quantity on one page; the price appears right there.

Upload your design to HyperFab and get a production price within minutes. For FDM 3D printing and laser cutting, the online estimator prices your part instantly.

## HyperFab at a glance

HyperFab (Persian: هایپرفب) is an online manufacturing platform in Tehran, Iran, offering FDM and resin 3D printing, CNC machining, metal and non-metal laser cutting and sheet metal bending, plus batch and industrial production. Customers upload a design file on hyperfab.ir: FDM 3D printing and laser cutting are priced instantly by the online price estimator, and other processes are quoted after an engineer reviews the file.

HyperFab’s 3D printing, CNC, laser and bending orders are usually ready within three working days, and the minimum order is one part. Parts are shipped across Iran by Post, Tipax and Snappbox, and pickup in Tehran is free. HyperFab’s Tekeyab service sources small pieces of industrial material — sheet, bar, shaft, flat bar, tube and profile in aluminium, stainless steel, steel, copper, brass and engineering plastics — quotes a price and cuts them to size if needed.

For industrial and batch production, HyperFab offers sheet and tube punching (metal and polyethylene), mould making and plastic injection moulding, batch CNC turning, custom aluminium extrusion, TIG and MIG welding, gold and silver plating and anodizing and powder coating. For punching, injection moulding and extrusion, tooling design and manufacture are part of the service, and parts are inspected before delivery. HyperFab’s engineering team comes from Iran’s top universities and has worked in industry for years. Industrial projects are handled by phone: +98 996 223 3898.

## Services and manufacturing processes

Every order is placed online: upload your design and get a price within minutes.

### FDM 3D Printing

FDM (Fused Deposition Modeling) 3D printing at HyperFab turns your 3D file into a plastic part, layer by layer, with no mould or tooling. You upload an STL or 3MF file on hyperfab.ir and the online price estimator instantly shows volume, weight, dimensions, print time and price. The calculation runs in your own browser, so the file is not sent anywhere until you place the order. PLA, PETG, ABS and TPU filaments are available, with layer heights from 0.1 to 0.3 mm.

FDM is the most economical additive manufacturing process and gives the best cost-to-result ratio for prototypes, spare parts that are no longer sold, workshop jigs and fixtures, architectural models and student projects. Before printing, every model is checked for wall thickness, orientation and weak points. The minimum order is a single part, quantity discounts are applied automatically, and parts are ready within three working days and shipped anywhere in Iran.
- File formats: STL · 3MF · OBJ · STEP
- Materials: PLA, PETG, ABS, TPU
- Layer height: 0.1 – 0.3 mm
- Pricing: Online, instant
- Lead time: Up to 3 working days

URL: https://hyperfab.ir/services/3d-printing/#fdm

### Resin 3D Printing (SLA / DLP)

Resin 3D printing (SLA / DLP) cures liquid resin layer by layer with ultraviolet light, giving far finer detail and a much smoother surface than FDM. HyperFab’s resin printing runs at 16K resolution, roughly 14 × 19 microns horizontally, and layer height is adjustable from 0.02 to 0.1 mm, so layer lines are almost invisible.

It is the first choice for small, precise parts: figures and miniatures, dental models, jewellery casting patterns, high-detail prototypes and display models. Three resins are available: standard resin for the highest detail, a tough engineering resin for parts that must take some impact, and a castable resin for investment-casting patterns. Resin print prices are based on resin volume and print time and are quoted after the file has been reviewed.
- Resolution: 16K — 14 × 19 µm XY
- Layer height: 0.02 – 0.1 mm
- Resins: Standard, Tough, Castable
- Pricing: After file review

URL: https://hyperfab.ir/services/3d-printing/#resin

### CNC Machining

CNC machining at HyperFab covers milling, turning, drilling, slotting and threading to your drawing, in engineering plastics and soft metals: polyethylene and acetal (POM / PE), PTFE (Teflon), nylon (PA6), acrylic (PMMA), Delrin (POM-C) and brass. Standard tolerance is ±0.05 mm, tighter tolerances are possible by arrangement, and surface finish is Ra 1.6 or better depending on material and tooling.

You upload a STEP or IGES model, a DWG or DXF drawing, or a dimensioned PDF on hyperfab.ir. The drawing is reviewed for tolerances, tool access to corners and manufacturability, then a price and lead time are quoted. Typical jobs include bushings, gears and rollers for machinery, PTFE seals and gaskets for chemical equipment, jigs and fixtures, clear acrylic enclosures and decorative brass parts. The minimum order is one part and lead time is up to three working days, depending on complexity.

CNC machining at HyperFab is not only for mould making. HyperFab makes all kinds of parts to customers’ drawings with high quality and precision, from single parts and prototypes to batch production of turned parts in brass and MO40 and CK45 steel.
- Operations: Milling, turning, drilling, slotting, threading
- Tolerance: ±0.05 mm
- Surface finish: Ra 1.6 or better
- File formats: STEP · IGES · DWG · DXF · PDF
- Pricing: After drawing review
- Batch production: Batch CNC turning

URL: https://hyperfab.ir/services/cnc/

### Metal Laser Cutting

HyperFab cuts mild steel, stainless steel, aluminium, galvanised and oiled sheet on a fibre laser with nitrogen assist gas, leaving a clean, oxide-free edge; CO₂ cutting is also available for general work. Cutting accuracy is ±0.1 mm with a kerf of about 0.15 mm, so outlines and hole positions match your file exactly and repeat from part to part.

Upload a DXF file on hyperfab.ir and the laser price estimator measures cut length, pierce count, sheet weight and bends directly from the drawing and gives a price instantly. At the same time it checks the drawing for duplicate lines, open contours, holes smaller than the sheet thickness and more than ten other common errors. Typical parts include brackets, machine panels and chassis, metal signs and logos, washers and plates, and sheet-metal prototypes. If the part also needs bending, cutting and bending are handled in one order.
- Laser: Fibre with nitrogen, and CO₂
- Accuracy: ±0.1 mm
- Kerf: About 0.15 mm
- File format: DXF
- Pricing: Online, instant

URL: https://hyperfab.ir/services/laser-metal/

### Non-metal Laser Cutting & Engraving

HyperFab cuts and engraves acrylic (Plexiglas), MDF, wood, leather, felt and foam on a CO₂ laser. Through-cutting, surface engraving and marking can be combined in one file and one run, and delicate lattice designs that a saw or router cannot reach are cut cleanly. Cutting accuracy is ±0.1 mm.

Send a vector DXF at 1:1 scale in millimetres, with cut lines and engraving areas on separate colours or layers. Typical jobs include custom boxes and packaging, architectural and teaching models, acrylic signs and logos, promotional items such as key rings and coasters, fabric and leather templates, and decorative panels. Single parts are welcome, and for larger runs the nesting on the sheet is optimised to lower the unit price.
- Laser: CO₂
- Accuracy: ±0.1 mm
- Operations: Cutting, engraving, marking
- File format: DXF
- Pricing: Online, instant

URL: https://hyperfab.ir/services/laser-nonmetal/

### Sheet Metal Bending

HyperFab bends sheet metal on a press brake with V-dies (air bending) to an angular accuracy of ±1°. Bending can be ordered on its own or as the next step after laser cutting. When cutting and bending are done in one order, lead time is shorter and bend positions line up more accurately with the holes.

Send the flat pattern as a DXF, a 3D STEP model or a dimensioned PDF; from a 3D model the correct flat pattern is calculated with the K-factor. Bend sequence, bend radius and tool clearance are checked before production so the sheet does not crack at the bend. Typical parts include L and U brackets, electrical cabinets and machine enclosures, chassis and frames for industrial equipment, cable trays and channels, façade panels and sheet-metal spare parts.
- Method: Press brake, V-die air bending
- Angle accuracy: ±1°
- File formats: DXF · STEP · PDF
- Combined service: Laser cutting and bending in one order

URL: https://hyperfab.ir/services/bending/

It has two calculation engines: an FDM 3D printing engine that analyses STL and 3MF files, and a laser cutting and sheet bending engine that reads DXF files. Both run inside your own browser. To get a price, your file is not sent to any server; it is uploaded only when you finalise the order, and only to make that order.

## Tekeyab: buy small pieces of industrial material without endless phone calls

Sheet, bar, shaft, flat bar, tube and profile in aluminium, stainless steel, steel, copper, brass and engineering plastics — in the size you need.

Need a small piece of aluminium sheet, a short length of stainless steel bar or one brass shaft, but suppliers only sell full lengths and whole sheets? Tekeyab is HyperFab’s online service for buying small pieces of industrial material. You describe the piece once in the Tekeyab form, and HyperFab sources it, quotes a price and cuts it to size if needed.

Tekeyab covers aluminium, stainless steel, carbon steel, copper and brass, engineering plastics and special metals, as sheet and plate, shaft and round bar, flat bar, tube and profile. Delivery is by courier in Tehran, in-person pickup, or shipping to other cities. If the piece is going to be machined, laser-cut or bent, you can order the fabrication in the same place.

- One form instead of ten calls: enter material, grade, shape, dimensions, quantity, when you need it and how to deliver it in a four-step form.
- Price in your account: after sourcing from suppliers, the final price is posted to your HyperFab account.
- Cut to size: the piece is cut to the requested size when needed and delivered ready to use.
- Tracking with a TK code: each request has a tracking code and its status, from sourcing to delivery, is visible in your account.

## Industrial and batch production: from moulds and turning to welding, plating and coating

A complete chain for batch parts, from production to final finish, with one responsible engineering team.

When a part moves from prototype to volume, the process has to change. For industrial and batch production, HyperFab offers a complete chain: sheet and tube punching, mould making and injection moulding, batch CNC turning, aluminium extrusion, welding and welded fabrication, plating and anodizing and powder coating. A part can go from production to final finish in one place.

HyperFab’s engineering team comes from Iran’s top universities, including Sharif University of Technology, and has worked in industry for years. It has taken four polyethylene injection moulds from build to commissioning, and more than 80,000 parts have been produced with them. Its record also includes quality control of 8,000 punched tubes, mating brass parts and MO40 and CK45 gauges, and stainless and aluminium structures for the medical and marine industries.

- Sheet and tube punching: metal and polyethylene; punching die design and manufacture and production runs.
- Mould making and injection moulding: mould making, sampling and production in PE, PP, ABS and nylon.
- Batch CNC turning: brass parts with fit tolerances and gauge parts in MO40 and CK45.
- Aluminium extrusion: your section with a dedicated die; you bring tonnage and die cost, we do the rest.
- TIG and MIG welding: stainless steel and 6000-series aluminium, welded structures and platforms, with VT, PT and PAUT.
- Plating and anodizing: silver and gold on brass and other metals, anodizing and chromate on aluminium.

## How it works

From file to finished part in four steps.

1. **You send the file**: A 3D model, a technical drawing, or even a photo and a description, uploaded on hyperfab.ir.
2. **An engineer reviews it**: Manufacturability, material, process and real dimensions are checked.
3. **Price and lead time are fixed**: Instant online for FDM and laser; after review for everything else. No hidden costs.
4. **We make and ship it**: With inspection before packing and delivery anywhere in Iran.

## FAQ

### What is HyperFab?

HyperFab (هایپرفب) is an online manufacturing platform in Tehran, Iran, offering FDM and resin 3D printing, CNC machining, metal and non-metal laser cutting and sheet metal bending. HyperFab also runs an instant online price estimator and the Tekeyab service for buying small pieces of industrial material. The main website and ordering are at hyperfab.ir.

### How do I get an online 3D printing price?

On hyperfab.ir, upload an STL or 3MF file in the order section. HyperFab’s estimator analyses the model in your browser and instantly shows the FDM price based on material, infill, layer height, scale and quantity. Resin printing is quoted after file review.

### How do I get a laser cutting price?

Upload the part’s DXF file at 1:1 scale in millimetres on hyperfab.ir and choose sheet material and thickness. The estimator measures cut length, pierce count, bends and sheet weight from the drawing and gives a price instantly.

### What is HyperFab Tekeyab?

Tekeyab is a service for buying small pieces of industrial material. You describe the piece in a form: material, shape, dimensions, quantity, when you need it and how to deliver it. HyperFab sources it from suppliers, quotes a price, cuts it to size if needed and ships it. Shapes include sheet, bar, shaft, flat bar, tube and profile, and materials include aluminium, stainless steel, steel, copper, brass and engineering plastics.

### How long does manufacturing take?

Most orders are ready within three working days. The exact time depends on the process, size and quantity. Shipping time is added to this and depends on the destination city and shipping method. Schedules for punching and injection moulding projects are agreed together with the quotation.

### Is there a minimum order quantity?

No. Even a single part is made. For larger quantities, a stepped discount is applied to the unit price automatically. For punching and injection moulding, which need tooling, HyperFab recommends the right process for your quantity and geometry.

### Does HyperFab do tube and sheet punching?

Yes. HyperFab punches sheet and tube in metal and polyethylene, including punching die design and manufacture and production runs. One example is kidney-shaped slots punched in polyethylene pipe with a 125 mm diameter, 5 mm wall and 6-bar pressure rating. Pricing is a die cost plus a cost per stroke, depending on the part’s geometry and material.

### Does HyperFab do mould making and plastic injection moulding?

Yes. HyperFab designs and builds injection moulds and produces and delivers plastic parts in a range of materials, including polyethylene, polypropylene, ABS and nylon. HyperFab’s team has taken four polyethylene injection moulds from build to commissioning, and more than 80,000 parts have been produced with them. Consultation is by phone: +98 996 223 3898.

### Does HyperFab ship outside Tehran?

Yes, anywhere in Iran via Post, Tipax and Snappbox. Pickup in Tehran is free.

### I don’t have a design file. What can I do?

Send a hand sketch, a photo of a sample part or a description of what it does. Design and 3D modelling are offered at a separate cost, and production starts after you approve the design. The order form also has an “I’m not sure / I want advice” option.

### Does HyperFab weld stainless steel and aluminium?

Yes. HyperFab does TIG and MIG welding of stainless steel and 6000-series aluminium and builds welded machine structures and large platform structures to the client’s drawings. VT, PT and PAUT testing is available on request, and many units have been built for the medical and marine industries.

### Does HyperFab do batch CNC turning?

Yes. HyperFab produces batch turned parts to drawing, including brass parts with fit tolerances and gauge parts in MO40 and CK45 steel. Each part’s critical points are engineered and checked before production.

### Does HyperFab extrude aluminium profiles?

Yes, as a specialisation and for aluminium only. Profiles are made in the customer’s own section with a dedicated die. The customer has the required tonnage and pays for the die, and HyperFab’s engineering team handles everything from section consultation to delivery.

### Does HyperFab do plating, anodizing and powder coating?

Yes, for production runs. HyperFab does silver and gold plating on brass and other metals, and anodizing and chromate (Alodine) on aluminium. Powder coating in powder, pearl, hammer and textured finishes is also available.

### Where is HyperFab and how do I contact it?

HyperFab’s order processing centre is at Unit 1, No. 39, corner of Tehrani Alley, Safi-Alishah St., Pich-e Shemiran, Enghelab St., Tehran, Iran. Phone +98 21 7752 7438; mobile, Bale and Telegram +98 996 223 3898; email info@hyperfab.ir. Hours are Saturday to Wednesday 9:00–17:00 and Thursday 9:00–13:00, Tehran time. Online ordering is open 24 hours.

# HyperFab Online Price Estimator — The price of your part, instantly

URL: https://hyperfabgroup.github.io/en/price-estimator/

The HyperFab Online Price Estimator is a free tool on hyperfab.ir that gives an instant price for FDM 3D printing from STL or 3MF files and for laser cutting and sheet bending from DXF files. It runs in your browser, so your file is not uploaded until you finalise the order, and the laser engine marks drawing errors before you pay. HyperFab is an online manufacturing platform in Tehran, Iran; resin 3D printing and CNC machining are quoted after an engineer reviews the file.

Upload a 3D file or a DXF drawing and see volume, weight, production time and price immediately. Everything is calculated in your browser, and your file is not sent anywhere to get a price.

- Service: Instant online quotes for FDM 3D printing and laser cutting and bending
- File formats: STL and 3MF for 3D printing; DXF for laser cutting and bending
- Cost: Free, with no obligation; an account is needed only to order
- Minimum order: One part; a minimum order value may apply
- Ordering: Online at hyperfab.ir, at any hour
- Location: HyperFab, Tehran, Iran

- FDM 3D printing: STL · 3MF
- Laser cutting and sheet bending: DXF
- Other processes: Resin and CNC quoted by an engineer after review

## What is the HyperFab price estimator?

The HyperFab price estimator (HyperFab Quote) is the online tool on hyperfab.ir that prices a manufactured part. You upload the part file, choose material, thickness, scale and quantity, and see the production price immediately, with no phone calls, no email back-and-forth and no waiting days for a quote.

It has two calculation engines: an FDM 3D printing engine that analyses STL and 3MF files, and a laser cutting and sheet bending engine that reads DXF files. Both run inside your own browser. To get a price, your file is not sent to any server; it is uploaded only when you finalise the order, and only to make that order.

The estimator’s price is not a rough guess. The printing engine slices the model by height like slicer software and calculates walls, infill and supports separately. The laser engine measures the real cut length, pierce count and bends from the drawing. No rate is hard-coded: every rate, from material price per kilo to the fee per bend, is set from HyperFab’s admin panel.

- **Price on the spot**: For FDM printing and laser cutting there is no waiting for a quote. Upload the file and see the price right away, even at 3 a.m.
- **Your file stays with you**: Geometry analysis and pricing run in your browser. The file is uploaded only when you finalise the order, and used only to make that order.
- **Drawing errors, before you pay**: An open contour, a duplicate line or a hole too small for the thickness is shown on the drawing before you order, not after a bad part is made.

## How is a 3D printing price calculated from an STL file?

A 3D print’s price depends above all on machine time and filament mass. HyperFab’s engine calculates both from your model’s real geometry.

- **Reads STL and 3MF**: The 3D model opens in your browser and its volume, dimensions, surface and cross-sections are extracted. A 3D preview of the part is shown on the same page.
- **Optimal bed orientation**: The engine evaluates different faces of the model and picks the orientation on the build plate that needs less support and prints more reliably.
- **Support analysis**: Overhanging surfaces are detected and the required support volume is estimated; supports cost both material and machine time.
- **Walls and infill, slice by slice**: The model is cut into successive slices. Each slice’s perimeter gives wall volume and its inner area gives infill volume, at the layer height and infill percentage you choose.
- **Filament mass and print time**: Volumes and nozzle speeds give filament mass and real machine time. Top and bottom skins are computed from the change in area between slices, so curved and stepped surfaces are not under-estimated.
- **Scale, quantity and discount**: Changing the scale updates the price instantly without re-uploading. As quantity rises, a stepped volume discount up to a set cap is applied to the unit price.

## How is laser cutting priced from a DXF file?

Each part of the price comes from a direct measurement of the drawing: cut length, pierce count, bends, engraving and sheet weight, plus setup and quantity. Upload a DXF at 1:1 scale in millimetres and choose sheet material and thickness. To order the part, see metal laser cutting and sheet metal bending on hyperfab.ir.

| Price component | How it is measured from the drawing |
|---|---|
| Cutting | Total cut length × sheet thickness, at a rate specific to each material, thickness and assist gas (oxygen or nitrogen) |
| Piercing | Number of points where the laser must pierce the sheet to start each contour |
| Bending | Number of bends and the length of each bend line, plus press-brake setup |
| Engraving | Length of engraving paths on the part |
| Material | Sheet weight from part area, thickness and material density, times price per kilo |
| Setup | A one-off fee per order, spread across the quantity rather than charged in full on every part |
| Quantity | Stepped discounts by quantity |

Note: because setup is spread across the quantity, the unit price genuinely drops at 20 or 40 parts; it does not depend on the discount alone.

## Which drawing errors does the estimator catch before you order?

Duplicate lines, open contours, holes smaller than the sheet thickness, holes too close to a bend line and other common errors. The laser estimator reviews the drawing like an experienced operator and marks every problem on the drawing itself.

- Duplicate overlapping lines: the same path would be cut twice and ruin the edge. Duplicates are excluded from the price.
- Open contour: an outline that does not close, so the part will not drop out of the sheet.
- Self-intersecting paths and no closed contour in the drawing.
- Hole smaller than sheet thickness: will not cut cleanly with a laser.
- Web thinner than the thickness: a narrow strip that warps or burns during cutting.
- Part larger than a standard sheet and machine capacity.
- Text, hatching and dimension lines left in the cutting drawing by mistake.
- Hole too close to a bend line: it will distort during bending.
- Short flange: an edge too short to sit on the bending tool.
- Sheet too thick to bend and bend longer than the press brake.
- Missing bending drawing when the part has bends.

## Which file formats does HyperFab accept, and how is each service priced?

FDM 3D printing and laser cutting are priced instantly by the estimator; resin 3D printing and CNC machining are quoted after an engineer reviews the file. For production runs of turned parts, see batch CNC turning; for small pieces of raw material, see Tekeyab.

| Process | File format | Pricing |
|---|---|---|
| FDM 3D printing | STL · 3MF (also OBJ, STEP) | Instant, with the estimator |
| Metal laser cutting | DXF | Instant, with the estimator |
| Non-metal laser cutting | DXF | Instant, with the estimator |
| Sheet metal bending | DXF · STEP · PDF | Bends priced from DXF; confirmed after the bending drawing is reviewed |
| Resin 3D printing | STL · OBJ · STEP · 3MF | After file review, by resin volume and print time |
| CNC machining | STEP · IGES · DWG · DXF · PDF | After drawing review, by material, stock removal and machine time |
| Not sure / advice | Any format, even a photo and description | After talking to an engineer |

## How do you order a part with an instant online quote?

Upload the file on hyperfab.ir, choose the specs, check the price and warnings, then order and track the part in your account.

1. **Upload the file**: On hyperfab.ir choose the process and upload an STL, 3MF or DXF file; the process is guessed from the file extension.
2. **Choose the specs**: Set material, colour, sheet thickness, layer height, infill, scale and quantity; the price updates with every change.
3. **See price and warnings**: Unit and total price are shown, together with manufacturability warnings on the drawing.
4. **Order and track**: Add the part to the cart and place the order. Its status appears under “Production orders” in your account.

## FAQ

### How does HyperFab calculate a 3D printing price?

HyperFab’s estimator analyses your STL or 3MF file in your browser. It places the model in the best orientation, estimates the supports needed, calculates wall and infill volume slice by slice, and derives filament mass and print time from these. The price comes from these two values and current rates, with a stepped discount for larger quantities.

### How do I get an online laser cutting quote?

Upload the part’s DXF file at 1:1 scale in millimetres on hyperfab.ir and choose sheet material and thickness. The estimator measures cut length, pierce count, bends, engraving and sheet weight from the drawing and shows the price immediately.

### Is my file sent to a server to calculate the price?

No. In HyperFab’s estimator, analysis and pricing run entirely in your own browser. The file is uploaded only when you finalise the order, and used only to make that order.

### Is the estimator’s price final?

The estimator’s price comes from your file’s real geometry and current rates, and it is the basis of the order. If the technical review before production finds an issue, HyperFab contacts you before production starts.

### Does the HyperFab estimator give instant prices for resin printing and CNC machining?

No. At HyperFab, resin printing and CNC machining depend on factors that need an engineer’s review, such as resin print orientation or the tooling and number of CNC operations. You upload the file and a price and lead time are quoted after review.

### Is the HyperFab price estimator free?

Yes. Getting a price is free and creates no obligation. You sign in to a HyperFab account only to place the final order.

### Why does print time determine a 3D printing price?

In 3D printing, the main cost is the time the machine spends building the part, not the weight of the plastic. Two parts of the same weight but different geometry can have very different print times and therefore very different prices. That is why HyperFab’s estimator calculates print time from the model’s real geometry.

### Is there a minimum order?

HyperFab has no minimum quantity; one part is accepted. A minimum order value may apply, and the estimator shows it clearly as a separate line.

### Which files can I upload to get an instant quote?

HyperFab’s estimator reads STL and 3MF files for FDM 3D printing and DXF files, at 1:1 scale in millimetres, for laser cutting and sheet bending. Resin printing files (STL, OBJ, STEP, 3MF) and CNC machining files (STEP, IGES, DWG, DXF, PDF) are quoted after review.

### Where is HyperFab and where do I get an instant quote?

HyperFab is an online manufacturing platform based in Tehran, Iran. Instant quotes are on hyperfab.ir in the order section, available at any hour; for advice, call +98 996 223 3898.

# Sheet and tube punching — From die design to production runs

URL: https://hyperfabgroup.github.io/en/punching/

Sheet and tube punching makes holes, slots and shaped cut-outs with a press stroke and a die, and is one of the fastest and most economical processes for repeat quantities. HyperFab, a manufacturing company in Tehran, Iran, punches metal and polyethylene sheet and tube, designs and builds the punching die, and runs production with quality control — including kidney-shaped slots in 125 mm polyethylene pipe. Pricing is a one-off die cost plus a cost per stroke, quoted after the drawing is reviewed; call +98 996 223 3898.

Holes, slots and custom shapes in metal and polyethylene sheet and tube. HyperFab designs and builds the punching die, runs a trial sample for your approval, and carries production through to delivery with full quality control.

- Service: Sheet and tube punching, punching die design and manufacture, production runs
- Materials: Metal and polymer sheet and tube, including polyethylene pipe
- Pricing model: One-off die cost plus cost per stroke, by geometry and material
- Quantity: Best for repeat runs; punching or laser cutting recommended by quantity and geometry
- Ordering: By phone (+98 996 223 3898) or Bale (@hyperfab_pro)
- Location: Tehran, Iran; parts shipped across Iran

- Punching: sheet and tube
- Materials: metals and polymers, including polyethylene
- Pricing: die cost + cost per stroke, by geometry and material

## What is sheet and tube punching?

Punching creates holes, slots and shaped cut-outs in sheet and tube with a press stroke and a die. For repeat quantities it is one of the fastest and most economical processes. Once the die is made, each part reaches its final shape in one or a few strokes, and every part comes out the same.

HyperFab handles punching end to end. The drawing is reviewed, a punching die is designed and built for the material and thickness, and a trial sample is punched for your approval. Production and quality control then run through to delivery. The service covers both sheet and tube, in metal and in polymers such as polyethylene, and punched parts can also be powder coated at HyperFab and delivered finished.

Punching polymer pipe is one of the hard jobs in this field. The pipe is round, the wall deforms under the stroke, and polyethylene behaves very differently from metal. HyperFab’s team has punched kidney-shaped slots in polyethylene pipe with a 125 mm diameter, 5 mm wall and 6-bar pressure rating. In another industrial project, the team was responsible for quality control of 8,000 punched tubes.

Punching or laser cutting? For low quantities or designs that keep changing, metal laser cutting is cheaper because there is no die cost. For repeat quantities, once the die is built, punching makes each part faster and cheaper. HyperFab offers both and recommends the right one for your quantity and geometry.

## What can HyperFab punch?

Metal and polymer sheet, metal tube and profile, and polyethylene pipe — with round and square holes, slots, kidney-shaped slots, perforated patterns and custom shapes to your drawing.

- **Metal sheet punching**: Round and square holes, slots, repeating patterns and custom shapes in mild steel, galvanised, stainless steel and aluminium sheet.
- **Metal tube and profile punching**: Holes and slots in metal tube and profile for structures, fittings, shelving, railings and furniture.
- **Polyethylene pipe punching**: Slots and holes in polyethylene pipe, including kidney-shaped slots, for drainage, filter and distribution pipes.
- **Polymer sheet punching**: Polyethylene and engineering-plastic sheet for gaskets, perforated plates and flat punched parts.
- **Custom shapes**: From a simple round hole to kidney slots, perforated patterns and special forms, exactly to your drawing.
- **Repeatable production runs**: Once the die is built, parts are produced with identical strokes and dimensions stay consistent from the first part to the last.

## How is punching priced?

Punching is priced as a one-off die cost plus a cost per stroke, quoted separately after the drawing is reviewed. Both depend on the part’s geometry and the material being punched.

| Cost component | What it depends on |
|---|---|
| Punching die (one-off) | Geometry and number of holes and slots, required accuracy, material and thickness, and whether the die is simple, progressive or tube-specific |
| Per stroke (production) | Material and thickness, strokes needed per part, and run quantity |
| Material | At current prices, if HyperFab supplies the sheet or tube |

Note: the tooling cost is paid once and spread across the run; the larger the quantity, the smaller the tooling share of each part’s price.

## Why choose HyperFab for a punching project?

Engineering review before the die is built, real tube-punching experience, and one owner from die design to delivery.

- **Engineering before the die**: The die is the most expensive part of the project. Before it is built, the design is reviewed from the die’s point of view: hole-to-edge distance, hole-diameter-to-thickness ratio and how the material behaves under the stroke. The goal is to build the die once, and build it right.
- **Real tube-punching experience**: From quality control of 8,000 punched tubes to kidney slots in 125 mm polyethylene pipe, we know the practical problems of this work first-hand.
- **Full responsibility to delivery**: From die design to the last stroke, the project has one owner: HyperFab. You approve a sample before production, and parts are inspected before delivery.

## How does a punching project work?

Send a drawing or sample with material, thickness and quantity; after engineering review and a quotation, the die is built and a trial sample is approved before production.

1. **Send drawing and specs**: Send the part drawing, material, thickness and quantity, or describe them by phone. A physical sample also works.
2. **Engineering review**: The design is checked for die manufacturability and changes are suggested where needed.
3. **Quotation**: Die cost and cost per stroke are quoted separately and clearly.
4. **Die and sample**: The die is built and a trial sample is punched for your approval before production.
5. **Production and delivery**: Parts are produced with dimensional quality control, packed and delivered.

## What is sheet and tube punching used for?

- Drainage and dewatering pipes with repeating slots or holes.
- Filter and strainer pipes, and water and air distribution pipes.
- Perforated plates, meshes and ventilation grilles.
- Flat punched parts for assembly such as washers, brackets and mounting plates.
- Housings and panels for industrial equipment with fixed hole patterns.
- Perforated profile and tube for structures, shelving and furniture.

# Mould making and plastic injection moulding — From part design to mass production

URL: https://hyperfabgroup.github.io/en/injection-molding/

Plastic injection moulding mass-produces plastic parts by injecting molten polymer into a steel mould, giving repeatable dimensions and, at high quantities, the lowest cost per part. HyperFab, a manufacturing company in Tehran, Iran, reviews the part for mouldability, designs and builds the injection mould, and runs production in polyethylene, polypropylene, ABS, nylon and other thermoplastics; its team has taken four polyethylene moulds to commissioning, producing more than 80,000 parts. Pricing is a one-off mould cost plus a cost per shot; call +98 996 223 3898.

Injection mould design and manufacture, and production runs of plastic parts in a range of materials. HyperFab carries the project from design review to delivery of finished parts, with controlled quality.

- Service: Injection mould design and manufacture, sampling and production runs
- Materials: PE, PP, ABS, nylon, polycarbonate, acetal and other thermoplastics
- Team experience: 4 polyethylene injection moulds to commissioning; 80,000+ parts produced
- Pricing model: One-off mould cost plus cost per shot, after design review
- Ordering: By phone (+98 996 223 3898) or Bale (@hyperfab_pro)
- Location: Tehran, Iran

- Services: mould design and manufacture, sampling, production runs
- Materials: polyethylene, polypropylene, ABS, nylon and other thermoplastics
- Pricing: mould cost + cost per shot

## What is injection moulding, and how does HyperFab handle it?

Injection moulding is the main process for mass-producing plastic parts. Molten polymer is injected under pressure into a steel mould, cools, and the part comes out with repeatable dimensions. At high quantities, no other process matches its cost per part and consistency.

An injection project succeeds or fails on the mould, and HyperFab starts there. First the part design is reviewed for mouldability. Then the mould is designed and built, and sampling and correction continue until the part is approved. Production runs follow, with quality control through to delivery.

HyperFab’s team has taken four polyethylene injection moulds from build supervision to commissioning, and more than 80,000 parts have been produced with them. That experience shows, before the mould is built, where a design is likely to cause trouble in production.

For smaller runs, 3D printing or CNC machining may be cheaper than a mould. HyperFab offers all three and recommends the right process after reviewing the project.

## What is checked before an injection mould is built?

Draft angles, wall thickness, ribs and bosses, gate location, undercuts and realistic tolerances are reviewed before tooling, because changing a design on paper costs almost nothing and changing a steel mould is expensive.

- Sufficient draft angle on walls, so the part releases without scuffing or sticking.
- Uniform wall thickness, so the part does not warp or show sink marks.
- Proper ribs and bosses instead of thick, material-heavy walls.
- Gate location, parting line and ejector pin positions.
- Undercuts and the need for slides or cores in the mould.
- Realistic tolerances for each material, allowing for polymer shrinkage.

## Which plastics can HyperFab injection mould?

Polyethylene, polypropylene, ABS, nylon and engineering thermoplastics such as polycarbonate and acetal; the material is recommended based on load, temperature, working environment and part cost.

- **Polyethylene (PE)**: Chemical- and impact-resistant; for caps, containers, fittings and industrial parts.
- **Polypropylene (PP)**: Light and fatigue-resistant; for living hinges, packaging and consumer parts.
- **ABS**: Good-looking surface and solid strength; for device housings and cosmetic parts.
- **Nylon (PA)**: Tough and wear-resistant; for gears, bushings and mechanical parts.
- **Engineering thermoplastics**: Polycarbonate, acetal (POM) and other materials, depending on the part’s use.
- **Choose the material with us**: Not sure? Describe the part’s use and a suitable material and grade will be recommended.

## How is injection moulding priced?

Injection moulding is priced as a one-off mould cost plus a cost per shot in production, quoted separately and clearly after the design is reviewed.

| Cost component | What it depends on |
|---|---|
| Mould (one-off) | Part size and complexity, number of cavities, undercuts and slides, surface finish and mould steel |
| Per shot (production) | Part material and weight, cycle time and run quantity |
| Material | Polymer type, grade and colour |

Note: the tooling cost is paid once and spread across the run; the larger the quantity, the smaller the tooling share of each part’s price.

## How does an injection moulding project work?

Send a 3D file, drawing or sample part; after a mouldability review and a quotation, the mould is built and sampled until you approve, then production runs.

1. **Send the design**: Send a 3D file, drawing or sample part. If you only have an idea, part design is available too.
2. **Mouldability review**: The design is checked for draft, wall thickness and parting line, and changes are suggested.
3. **Quotation**: Mould cost and cost per shot are quoted separately and clearly.
4. **Mould and sampling**: The mould is built, sampled and corrected until you give final approval.
5. **Production and delivery**: Parts are produced with quality control and delivered.

Before investing in a mould: you can make a prototype with HyperFab FDM 3D printing and check form, dimensions and assembly on a real part.

## Why choose HyperFab for an injection moulding project?

Engineering review before tooling, real production experience and one owner from design to delivery.

- **Engineering before tooling**: HyperFab’s engineering team comes from Iran’s top universities and has worked at the heart of industry for years. It reviews your design from a production point of view before the mould is built, so the mould is built once, and built right.
- **Real production experience**: Four injection moulds from build supervision to commissioning and more than 80,000 parts produced; we know the road from design to mass production first-hand.
- **One owner from design to delivery**: From the mould to the last part, full responsibility for the project lies with HyperFab. You approve samples before production and quality is checked before delivery.

HyperFab prices them in two main parts: a one-off mould cost and a cost per shot in production. The mould cost depends on part size and complexity, number of cavities and undercuts. ### Is there a minimum quantity for injection moulding?

# CNC turning of industrial parts — Production runs with proven precision

URL: https://hyperfabgroup.github.io/en/cnc-turning/

Batch CNC turning is the production of rotational parts — shafts, bushings, pins, nozzles, fittings and mating parts — in runs where every part must be as good as the approved first article. HyperFab, a manufacturing company in Tehran, Iran, produces batch turned parts to drawing in brass, MO40 (42CrMo4) and CK45 (C45) steel and other metals, with each part’s critical points engineered before production. Pricing is by material, complexity, tolerances and quantity and is quoted after drawing review; call +98 996 223 3898.

Batch production of turned parts in brass, MO40 alloy steel, CK45 steel and other metals, to drawing and with precise fit tolerances. The critical points of every part are engineered and checked before production, from the first sample to the last part of the run.

- Service: Batch CNC turning to drawing, for production runs
- Materials: Brass, MO40 (42CrMo4), CK45 (C45), stainless steel, aluminium and other metals
- Quality control: First-article approval and dimensional inspection
- Pricing model: By material, complexity, tolerances and quantity, after drawing review
- Ordering: By phone (+98 996 223 3898) or Bale (@hyperfab_pro)
- Location: Tehran, Iran

- For: production runs
- Materials: brass, MO40 (42CrMo4), CK45 (C45) and other metals
- Precision: fit tolerances, mating parts and gauges

## What is batch CNC turning?

CNC turning is the main way to make rotational parts: shafts, bushings, pins, nuts, nozzles, fittings and parts that must fit precisely into each other. In batch production, the real challenge is not making one good part. It is making hundreds or thousands of parts that are all exactly that good part.

HyperFab has produced batch turned parts for a long time. They range from brass parts with fit tolerances that must mate with each other to gauge parts in MO40 alloy steel and CK45 steel. They were made to high precision and approved by the customers.

Behind that precision is engineering before turning. Before production starts, each part’s critical points are engineered and briefed to the machinist: fit surfaces, critical diameters, concentricity and surface finish at specific points. The machinist then knows exactly where the part needs which accuracy. For each part, the production method and precision level are chosen to match its requirements — no more expensive than needed, never below requirements.

For production runs only: this service is for batch production; one-off parts are accepted only rarely. A suitable quantity is recommended after reviewing the project.

## Which materials and parts does HyperFab turn?

Brass, MO40 (42CrMo4) and CK45 (C45) steel, stainless steel, aluminium and other metals — for mating parts, gauges, shafts, pins, bushings and fittings.

- **Brass parts**: Brass bushings, nozzles, fittings, pins and mating parts with fit tolerances and a clean finish.
- **MO40 steel (42CrMo4)**: Chromium-molybdenum alloy steel for loaded parts and gauges, with high strength and toughness.
- **CK45 steel (C45)**: Medium-carbon steel for shafts, pins, machine parts and gauges.
- **Gauge parts**: Dimensional inspection gauges that are themselves the precision reference of a production line.
- **Mating parts**: Sliding and press fits between parts, with control of critical diameters and concentricity.
- **Other metals**: Stainless steel, aluminium and other steels, depending on the project.

## How is precision held across a production run?

By engineering the drawing before production, briefing the machinist on every critical point, approving a first article and inspecting dimensions during production and before delivery.

- Drawing engineering before production: identifying fit surfaces, critical dimensions and measurement datums.
- Technical briefing for the machinist: the accuracy of each critical point, the operation sequence and the measurement method.
- Precision matched to requirements: the precision level and cost are set by each part’s importance — no more than needed, no less.
- First-article approval before the production run starts.
- Dimensional inspection during production and before delivery.
- Suitable packing so precision fit surfaces are not damaged.

## Can turned parts be plated, coated or welded?

Yes. A turned part usually needs a finish or assembly too. At HyperFab you can include silver and gold plating, anodizing and chromate, powder coating and welding in the same project, and receive the finished, ready-to-use part.

For one-off parts and prototypes, see CNC machining on the HyperFab website.

## How does a batch turning order work?

Send a dimensioned drawing with tolerances, the material and the quantity; after engineering review and a quotation, a first article is made for your approval before the run starts.

1. **Send the drawing**: Send a dimensioned drawing with tolerances, the material and the quantity, or describe them by phone.
2. **Engineering review**: Fit surfaces and critical dimensions are identified and production notes are set.
3. **Quotation**: Priced by material, complexity, tolerances and quantity.
4. **First article**: The first part is made and inspected; the run starts after your approval.
5. **Production and delivery**: The run is produced with dimensional inspection and delivered.

# Aluminium profile extrusion — Your cross-section, with a dedicated die

URL: https://hyperfabgroup.github.io/en/aluminium-extrusion/

Custom aluminium extrusion makes long aluminium profiles with your own constant cross-section by pushing a hot billet through a dedicated steel die. HyperFab, a manufacturing company in Tehran, Iran, specialises in aluminium extrusion: you bring the required tonnage and pay for the die, and HyperFab’s engineering team handles section consultation, die making, profile production, quality control and delivery. Die cost and profile price are quoted separately; call +98 996 223 3898.

Aluminium profiles in the cross-section you need. HyperFab’s engineering team advises on the section geometry, then a dedicated extrusion die is built and the profile is produced. You need the required tonnage and pay for the die; HyperFab’s engineering team handles the rest.

- Service: Custom aluminium profile extrusion with a dedicated die
- Material: Aluminium only
- Minimum order: By tonnage, advised after section consultation
- Pricing model: Die cost plus profile price by alloy, weight and tonnage, quoted separately
- Ordering: By phone (+98 996 223 3898) or Bale (@hyperfab_pro)
- Location: Tehran, Iran

- Speciality: aluminium extrusion only
- Your part: required tonnage + die cost
- Our part: section consultation, die, production, QC and delivery

## What is aluminium extrusion?

Aluminium extrusion pushes a hot aluminium billet under pressure through a steel die to make a long profile with a constant cross-section. Almost any section you can draw can be made with a dedicated die: solid, hollow, slotted, finned or with screw ports. That makes extrusion the most economical way to make long, uniform aluminium parts.

HyperFab specialises in aluminium extrusion. The model is simple: you bring the required tonnage and pay for the die. Section design consultation, die making, profile production, quality control and delivery are handled by HyperFab’s engineering team. The result is a profile with exactly the section you need, not the closest one available on the market.

Consultation before the die matters. Extrusion dies are expensive, and a poorly designed section can lead to warped profiles, uneven surfaces or a broken die. Before the die is made, HyperFab’s engineering team reviews your section for wall thickness, symmetry, corner radii and tongue ratios and suggests changes, so the die is built once, and built right.

Aluminium only: in extrusion, HyperFab works exclusively with aluminium. Orders are by tonnage, and the right tonnage for each section is advised after consultation.

## Who does what in a custom extrusion order?

You define the use, approve the section and pay for the die; HyperFab designs and builds the die, produces the profile at the ordered tonnage and handles quality control and delivery.

| Step | Who |
|---|---|
| Defining the use and initial section | You |
| Consultation and final section geometry | HyperFab’s engineering team, with your approval |
| Paying for the die | You |
| Extrusion die design and manufacture | HyperFab |
| Profile production at the ordered tonnage | HyperFab |
| Quality control and delivery | HyperFab |

## Which aluminium profiles can HyperFab extrude?

Industrial and T-slot profiles, heat sinks, housings and enclosures, architectural profiles, hollow sections and rails — each in your own cross-section.

- **Industrial and T-slot profiles**: Structural and slotted profiles for machine frames, workbenches and production lines.
- **Heat sinks and finned profiles**: Finned profiles for heat dissipation in power electronics, drives and LEDs.
- **Housings and enclosures**: Device housings and electronic enclosures with a section dedicated to your product.
- **Architectural and decorative profiles**: Frames, edges, handles and decorative profiles.
- **Hollow and multi-cavity profiles**: Hollow and multi-cavity sections that are both light and strong.
- **Rails and guides**: Rails, linear guides and light parts for equipment and transport.

## How should an extrusion section be designed?

Keep walls uniform, round sharp corners, balance the section and control slot depth: these extend die life and lower the cost per kilo, and all of them are reviewed in consultation.

- Uniform wall thickness: large thickness differences unbalance metal flow and warp the profile.
- Rounded corners: give sharp corners a small radius for longer die life and a better surface.
- Balanced section: symmetric, balanced sections extrude more stably and accurately.
- Die tongues: deep, narrow slots weaken the die tongue; the depth-to-width ratio must be controlled.
- Section size: the section must fit the production range; the right size is set in consultation.
- Tolerances: keep tight tolerances for functional dimensions only.

## Can extruded profiles be anodized, coated or machined?

Yes. An extruded profile is usually not yet the finished product. At HyperFab you can add aluminium anodizing, powder coating, machining, punching and aluminium welding, and receive a part that is ready to assemble.

## How is a custom aluminium profile ordered and priced?

After section consultation, the die cost and the profile price — by alloy, weight and tonnage — are quoted separately; a sample profile is approved before production.

1. **Send the section or idea**: Send the section drawing, a DXF or even a sketch and the profile’s use, or describe it by phone.
2. **Section consultation**: The engineering team reviews and optimises the section for extrusion and advises the right tonnage.
3. **Quotation**: Die cost and profile price, by alloy, weight and tonnage, are quoted separately.
4. **Die and sample**: The die is built and a sample profile is produced for your approval.
5. **Production and delivery**: The profile is produced at the ordered tonnage, inspected and delivered.

Yes, as a specialisation: aluminium profiles in the customer’s own cross-section, with a dedicated die. Section consultation, die making, production and delivery are handled by HyperFab’s engineering team.

### What do I need to order a custom aluminium profile?

The required tonnage and payment for the die. To start, send the section drawing, a DXF or a sketch and the profile’s use. The section is finalised after consultation with HyperFab’s engineering team, which also handles everything else, from die making to profile delivery.

## TIG or MIG welding for stainless steel and aluminium?

TIG gives clean, precise welds on thin sheet and sensitive parts; MIG is faster for long and structural welds. HyperFab does both on stainless steel and 6000-series aluminium.

Argon-shielded welding — TIG (GTAW) and MIG (GMAW) — is the main way to join stainless steel and 6000-series aluminium in machine and equipment building.

HyperFab’s work is not just laying welds; it is building and assembling the project from drawing to delivery. That covers cutting and preparing parts, fixturing, welding with distortion control, weld finishing and testing. HyperFab has built many units for the medical and marine industries, where weld cleanliness and corrosion resistance are critical.

The experience goes beyond small parts. HyperFab has built large platform structures, including a framed chassis mounted on wheels that runs on rails — a structure where flatness, alignment and dimensional accuracy over long lengths decide everything.

If a welded part also needs a finish, it can be powder coated at HyperFab and delivered as a finished part in one place. Flat sheet parts can also be ordered through metal laser cutting on hyperfab.ir.

## Does HyperFab design the welded structure?

Anything worth flagging is discussed with you before fabrication.

For large and platform structures, complete approved drawings are essential before fabrication starts. HyperFab takes responsibility for fabrication, follow-up and quality control through to delivery.

## Which weld tests are available?

Visual testing (VT), liquid penetrant testing (PT), phased-array ultrasonic testing (PAUT) and other tests, carried out on request to suit the project’s requirements.

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| VT — visual testing | Weld shape and size, surface cracks, undercut, spatter and visible defects |
| PT — liquid penetrant | Surface-breaking cracks and discontinuities; suited to non-magnetic stainless steel and aluminium |
| PAUT — phased-array ultrasonics | Internal weld defects such as lack of fusion, internal cracks and porosity, with a cross-section image of the weld |
| Other tests | As the project and client require |

4. **Fabrication and welding**: Parts are prepared, fixtured, welded and finished as needed.
5. **Testing and delivery**: Requested tests are carried out and the structure is delivered.

## Does HyperFab do gold plating, silver plating and anodizing?

Yes. HyperFab does silver and gold plating on brass and other metals, and anodizing and chromate conversion (Alodine) on aluminium, for production runs.

Surface finish is the last and most visible step in making a part. It sets the part’s appearance and its resistance to corrosion and wear, and its electrical behaviour.

The service covers both decorative and technical parts. For decorative parts, a bright, lasting appearance matters: décor items, hardware, statuettes and corporate gifts. ## Which plating and anodizing finishes are available?

Silver plating, gold plating, aluminium anodizing and chromate (Alodine), on brass, aluminium and other metals.

- **Silver plating**: The highest electrical conductivity of any metal; for contacts, connectors, busbars and electrical parts, and for decorative items with a bright silver look.
- **Gold plating**: Excellent resistance to oxidation and stable contact resistance; for connectors and electronics, and for jewellery, hardware and luxury items.
- **Aluminium anodizing**: A hard oxide layer grown on aluminium that raises corrosion and wear resistance; for housings, profiles and industrial and decorative parts.
- **Chromate (Alodine)**: A thin conversion coating on aluminium that prevents corrosion, keeps the surface electrically conductive and makes a good paint base.
- **On brass and other metals**: Plating on brass and other metals, from turned parts to castings and sheet parts.
- **Consistent across the run**: The same preparation and checks for every part in a batch, so colour and appearance match from first part to last.

## Silver, gold, anodizing or chromate: which finish suits your part?

Silver for the highest conductivity, gold for oxidation resistance and stable contact resistance, anodizing for a hard, corrosion- and wear-resistant layer on aluminium, and chromate for a conductive, paintable surface on aluminium.

| Finish | Base metal | Main property | Typical uses |
|---|---|---|---|
| Silver plating | Brass, copper and other metals | Highest conductivity, silver appearance | Contacts and connectors, busbars, RF parts, decorative items |
| Gold plating | Brass, copper and other metals | Oxidation-resistant, stable contact resistance, gold appearance | Connectors and electronics, jewellery, luxury hardware |
| Anodizing | Aluminium | Hard oxide layer, corrosion- and wear-resistant | Housings, profiles, industrial and decorative parts |
| Chromate (Alodine) | Aluminium | Corrosion protection with a conductive surface, paint base | Electronic parts, enclosures, parts before painting |

## What are plating and anodizing used for?

- Electrical and electronic parts: contacts, connectors, terminals and busbars with silver or gold plating.
- Decorative items and gifts: statuettes, badges, hardware and décor with gold and silver plating.
- Device housings and frames: anodized or chromated aluminium parts, including custom aluminium extrusion profiles.
- Turned brass parts: fittings and precision parts with protective or decorative plating.
- Aluminium parts before painting: chromate as an adhesion base, for example before powder coating.

## FAQ

### Does HyperFab do gold and silver plating?

### Does HyperFab anodize aluminium?

Yes. HyperFab does anodizing and chromate conversion (Alodine) on aluminium parts, for production runs.

### What is chromate or Alodine?

Chromate is a thin conversion coating on aluminium that prevents corrosion and, unlike anodizing, keeps the surface electrically conductive. It is also a good paint base. Alodine is the well-known trade name of this kind of coating.

### Silver or gold plating — which is better?

Silver has the highest conductivity and costs less but tarnishes over time in air. Gold conducts less but does not oxidise, so its contact resistance stays stable. The choice depends on use, environment and budget.

# Powder coating (electrostatic, oven-cured) — Durable finishes for batch parts

URL: https://hyperfabgroup.github.io/en/powder-coating/

Powder coating is a dry, electrostatically charged powder that is oven-cured into a hard, even layer, more durable than liquid paint. HyperFab, a manufacturing company in Tehran, Iran, powder-coats batch parts in steel, iron, aluminium and other metals, in standard, pearl, hammer and textured finishes, gloss or matt, in a wide range of colours including RAL codes. Pricing depends on part size and surface area, finish, preparation and quantity and is quoted after review; call +98 996 223 3898.

- Finishes: powder, pearl, hammer, texture, gloss and matt
- On: steel, iron, aluminium and other metals
- For: production runs

## What is powder coating?

Powder coating applies a dry powder to a metal part. The electrically charged powder clings to the part, which is then cured in an oven so the powder melts into a continuous, hard layer. The result is thicker, more even and more resistant to impact, scratches and corrosion than liquid paint.

HyperFab powder-coats batch metal parts with high quality at a fair price: machine housings and chassis, structures, industrial parts and consumer products. If the part is also made at HyperFab — by punching, welding or turning — you receive the coated, finished part in one place. On aluminium, chromate conversion as a base improves paint adhesion.

For production runs only: this service is for batch production; one-off parts are accepted only rarely. A suitable quantity is recommended after reviewing the project.

## Which powder coating finishes are available?

Electrostatic powder, pearl, hammer, texture and wrinkle finishes, in gloss, satin or matt and a wide range of colours, including standard RAL codes.

- **Electrostatic powder**: The most common powder coating: an even, solvent-free finish with strong adhesion and durability.
- **Pearl (metallic and pearlescent)**: A metallic or pearlescent sheen for cosmetic parts, décor and premium products.
- **Hammer finish**: A texture like hammered metal that hides imperfections; common on machine housings, cabinets and tools.
- **Texture and wrinkle**: A rough, matt surface that hides fingerprints and scratches; for high-touch parts.
- **Gloss, satin and matt**: The gloss level to suit the use and look of the product.
- **Wide colour range**: A wide range of colours, including standard RAL codes.

## How does powder coating work, step by step?

Surface preparation, electrostatic powder application, oven curing, then inspection and delivery.

1. **Surface preparation**: Degreasing and cleaning, plus other preparation where needed for better adhesion.
2. **Powder application**: Charged powder is sprayed evenly onto the part.
3. **Oven curing**: The part is cured in an oven so the powder melts into a hard, continuous layer.
4. **Inspection and delivery**: Appearance and evenness are checked and parts are packed and delivered.

## What is powder coating used for?

- Machine housings and chassis and industrial equipment.
- Electrical cabinets, enclosures and metal boxes.
- Metal structures, shelving and racks.
- Metal furniture and décor.
- Car and motorcycle parts, wheels and body parts.
- Home appliances and metal consumer products.

## Powder coating or ordinary paint: which lasts longer?

Powder coating gives a thicker, harder layer that lasts longer than ordinary liquid paint against impact, scratches and corrosion.

- **More durable**: A thicker, harder layer that lasts longer against impact, scratches and corrosion.
- **Consistent across the run**: The same thickness and look on every part in a batch, with no runs or blotches.
- **Many looks**: From matt and gloss to pearl, hammer and textured, for every taste and use.

# 3D Printing vs CNC vs Injection Moulding: Choosing by Quantity

URL: https://hyperfabgroup.github.io/en/guides/3d-printing-vs-cnc-vs-injection/
Updated: 2026-11-15

For one to a few parts, 3D printing is usually the cheapest and quickest option. For tens to hundreds, choose between 3D printing and CNC machining based on material, geometry and accuracy. Once you need thousands, the mould cost spreads across the run and injection moulding gives the lowest cost per part.

## 3D printing vs CNC vs injection moulding: what is the difference?

These three processes follow very different cost logic. 3D printing builds a part layer by layer straight from a file, with no tooling at all. CNC machining cuts the part out of a solid block by milling and turning. Injection moulding (injection molding in US spelling) forces molten polymer into a steel mould, and every shot produces one or more identical parts.

The key difference is set-up cost. 3D printing has almost none, CNC needs programming and fixturing, and injection moulding cannot start until a mould has been designed and built. In return, the cost per moulded part falls steeply as quantity rises, while the cost per printed part stays roughly flat.

| Factor | 3D printing | CNC machining | Injection moulding |
|---|---|---|---|
| Set-up cost | Almost none; no tooling | Low; programming and fixturing | High; mould design and build |
| Cost per part as quantity rises | Roughly flat; stepped discounts only | Falls a little | Falls steeply |
| Typical quantity | One to tens | One to hundreds | Thousands and up |
| Materials at HyperFab | PLA, PETG, ABS, TPU and resins | PE, acetal, PTFE, nylon, acrylic, brass | PE, PP, ABS, nylon, polycarbonate, acetal |
| Accuracy and finish | Fine for prototypes; resin gives finer detail | Tightest control of size and finish | Repeatable; depends on mould and shrinkage |
| Design changes | Easy; swap the file | Easy; edit the program | Costly; the mould must be modified |
| How HyperFab prices it | FDM instantly online at hyperfab.ir | After drawing review | Mould cost plus cost per shot, by phone |

## Cheapest way to make one to a few parts

When you need a single prototype or a handful of parts, set-up cost dominates. FDM 3D printing is almost always the cheapest option here because there is no mould and no machining program: your STL or 3MF file goes straight to the printer. HyperFab’s minimum order is one part, and the online price estimator on hyperfab.ir shows the FDM price the moment you upload.

For small parts with fine detail or a smooth surface, such as display models or precise assembly parts, resin printing (SLA / DLP) gives a better result. If the part must be made from a real engineering material such as PTFE, acetal or brass, or needs threads and accurate sealing faces, CNC machining makes sense even for a single piece.

## Tens to hundreds of parts: 3D printing or CNC?

In this range, geometry and material matter more than the count. 3D printing suits complex shapes, internal cavities and organic forms, because complexity adds little to the cost. Stepped discounts lower the unit price, but every part still needs its own print time and material.

CNC machining wins on simpler, prismatic parts such as bushings, washers, rollers and fixtures, and wherever the real material and dimensional accuracy matter. Once the program is written, its set-up cost is shared across the batch. For turned metal parts in larger quantities, such as brass fittings, HyperFab’s batch CNC turning is a separate service.

## At what quantity does injection moulding pay off?

Once you need thousands of parts or more, injection moulding is usually the most economical process. The mould is paid for once and its cost is spread across every part. After that, the cost per part depends mainly on material, part weight and cycle time.

Moulding also brings consistency: the last part matches the first. At HyperFab, an injection project starts with a mouldability review of the design, and the mould cost and cost per shot are quoted separately. These projects are arranged by phone rather than through online ordering.

## How material and accuracy change the choice

Quantity is not the only factor; sometimes the material decides for you. If the part must be brass, PTFE or acetal, 3D printing is no real substitute and CNC is the natural route. If you need polyethylene or polypropylene parts in high volumes, injection moulding gives you that material at a lower cost.

Accuracy differs too. CNC gives the most control over dimensions and surface finish, which suits mating faces and bearing seats. Injection moulding is highly repeatable, but final accuracy depends on mould design and polymer shrinkage. FDM parts show layer lines and are weaker across the layers.

## Break-even between processes, explained without numbers

The logic is simple even without figures. Each process has a fixed cost (tooling, mould, programming) and a variable cost (price per part times quantity). 3D printing has almost no fixed cost and a higher variable cost. Injection moulding is the opposite: a high fixed cost and a low cost per part. CNC sits in between.

Plot total cost against quantity for each process and the lines cross somewhere; that crossing is the break-even point. Below it, the tool-free process is cheaper; above it, the mould pays for itself. Where the lines cross is different for every part, so it has to be worked out project by project. Before you decide, answer these questions:

- What is the total volume over the product’s life, not just the first order?
- Is the design frozen, or is it still likely to change?
- What material does the part need, and what load, temperature or environment must it handle?
- Which dimensions are truly critical, and what surface finish do you need?
- Is the geometry complex, or simple and prismatic?

## What affects the cost of each process?

None of these processes can be priced without seeing the file or drawing, but the main cost drivers are clear:

- 3D printing: material volume and weight, print time, layer height, infill, filament or resin type, and quantity.
- CNC machining: stock material and size, number of operations and set-ups, tolerances and surface finish, and quantity.
- Injection moulding, the mould: part size and complexity, number of cavities, undercuts and slides, surface finish and mould steel.
- Injection moulding, production: part material and weight, cycle time and run quantity.

For FDM 3D printing, upload your file to the online price estimator at hyperfab.ir and see the price now; for CNC, upload your model or drawing there too and receive a quote after review. For mould making and injection moulding, or if you are unsure which process fits your quantity, call 09962233898 and HyperFab will review the design and recommend a process with an exact quote.

## FAQ

### Which process is cheapest for ten pieces?

For ten pieces, FDM 3D printing is usually cheapest because there is no set-up cost, and you can see the price instantly in the online estimator on hyperfab.ir. If the part must be an engineering material such as PTFE or brass, or needs high accuracy, CNC machining is the better choice. A mould is not worth building for that quantity.

### When does an injection mould pay off?

When the saving per part, multiplied by the total quantity, exceeds the cost of building the mould. That point depends on part size, complexity and material, and it usually falls at high volumes. HyperFab quotes the mould cost and the cost per shot separately after reviewing the design, so you can compare.

### Are 3D-printed parts strong enough?

For prototypes, jigs, fixtures and many functional parts under moderate load, yes, especially in PETG or ABS with the right print orientation. FDM parts are weaker across the layers, so for heavy loads or constant wear a part machined from nylon or acetal, or an injection-moulded part, is the safer choice.

### Can I switch methods later?

Yes, and that is the usual path: prototype with 3D printing, make small batches by printing or CNC, then move to injection moulding. If the design includes draft, uniform wall thickness and ribs from the start, it can move to a mould without a redesign.
